title: KAMP
text: Hello welcome KAMP package! package designed calculate expectation variance KAMP (K adjustment Analytical Moments Permutation distribution) point patterns marks. package partially built spatstat package, powerful tool analyzing spatial data R. KAMP package provides functions simulate point patterns, calculate KAMP CSR, visualize results. package designed user-friendly easy use, focus providing clear concise output. package still development, welcome feedback suggestions improvement. questions issues, please feel free reach us.

title: KAMP
text: concepts come throughout vignette: ppp object: spatstat’s representation point pattern – set point locations (x/y coordinates) inside bounding window, optionally marks attribute labeling point (e.g. cell type). kamp() can build one plain data.frame, can pass one directly. Ripley’s K function: measure spatial clustering. given radius r, K(r) roughly captures expected number additional points within distance r typical point, normalized point density. Values higher expected randomness indicate clustering; lower values indicate dispersion (points spread expected). Complete spatial randomness (CSR): null hypothesis points distributed independently uniformly random. theoretical K CSR (theo_csr) assumes homogeneous point density across whole window – assumption ’s often violated real tissue images (e.g. due holes, folds, regions cells). KAMP: Rather comparing observed K theoretical CSR baseline, KAMP computes expectation variance K permutation null – ’d see marks randomly reassigned among existing point locations. adapts actual inhomogeneity tissue. KAMP computes permutation distribution’s moments analytically (closed form) instead simulating many permutations, stays fast even large datasets.

title: KAMP
text: can use kamp() function calculate KAMP expectation univariate data. kamp() function several parameters allow us customize calculation: df: Either point pattern object created using ppp() function spatstat package, plain data.frame x/y columns marks column (case mark_var required). rvals: sequence distances calculate K function. univariate: logical value indicating whether calculate univariate K function (default TRUE). mark_var: name marks column df, df data.frame. Ignored df already ppp object. mark1: value marks variable first mark (required univariate). mark2: value marks variable second mark (optional univariate). variance: logical value indicating whether calculate variance (default FALSE). correction: edge correction use – "trans"/"translational" (default), "iso"/"isotropic", "none". thin: logical value indicating whether use thinning (default FALSE). p_thin: Percentage thin (default 0.5). univariate data, need specify one marks variable. case, set univariate = TRUE variance = FALSE (default). univariate = TRUE calculates K function one mark versus background. variance = FALSE means compute expectation. correction uses translational correction default. Choosing correction: edge correction matters points near window’s boundary fewer visible neighbors points interior, can bias K downward larger radii left uncorrected. "trans"/"translational" (default): good default cases; reweights pair points much window overlaps shifted separation vector. "iso"/"isotropic": another commonly-used correction; can behave differently irregularly-shaped windows computationally expensive. "none": correction – fastest option, biased whenever edge effects aren’t negligible (e.g. large r relative window’s size, small/irregular window).

title: KAMP: Permutation-Based Ripley's K Analysis for Spatial Point Patterns
text: KAMP R package efficiently estimating Ripley’s K complete spatial randomness using robust statistical approach called KAMP (K adjusted Analytical Moments Permutation distribution). Rather repeatedly permuting marks across point pattern simulating null distribution – traditional way get permutation-based null K – KAMP computes permutation distribution’s mean variance analytically, closed form. gives permutation-adapted baseline (one accounts spatial inhomogeneity, unlike standard theoretical CSR baseline) without computational cost actually running permutations, making suitable large-scale spatial analyses encountered spatial proteomics multiplex imaging datasets.
